rules.title: Limit nonmetallic wireway to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict nonmetallic wireways to the environments and configurations for which they are suited and identified.
evidence_required: Plan/spec showing wireway run as exposed work
Listing/identification mark for wet or corrosive use where applicable
Detail showing unbroken length and conductor access on both sides at any wall pass-through

rules.title: Prohibit nonmetallic wireway in unsuitable locations
rules.intent: Prevent use of nonmetallic wireways where physical, thermal, environmental, or hazard conditions exceed their listing.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming no hazardous (classified) area or physical-damage exposure
Listing mark for sunlight resistance where exposed to sun
Conductor insulation temperature rating vs wireway listed temperature comparison

rules.title: Group parallel conductors to balance current
rules.intent: Prevent current imbalance from inductive reactance in paralleled conductors.
evidence_required: One-line / cable schedule showing parallel conductor grouping per phase, neutral, and grounded conductor
Confirmation parallel arrangement complies with 310.10(G)

rules.title: Limit conductor fill to 20 percent
rules.intent: Prevent overheating and damage by limiting cross-sectional fill of the wireway.
evidence_required: Conductor fill calculation showing total conductor area <= 20% of interior cross-sectional area
Wireway interior cross-sectional area from listing/marking
Conductor schedule identifying any excluded signaling or motor-starting conductors

rules.title: Apply deflection and pull-box dimensions to insulated conductors
rules.intent: Ensure adequate bending space and pull distances to avoid conductor insulation damage.
evidence_required: Wireway dimension detail at deflection points meeting Table 312.6(A) one-wire-per-terminal spacing
Pull calculation for 4 AWG and larger conductors against 314.28(A)(1)/(2)
Raceway/trade-size transposition for cables used as straight/angle pulls

rules.title: Support nonmetallic wireway at required intervals
rules.intent: Maintain mechanical integrity and prevent sag or joint failure.
evidence_required: Support layout showing horizontal intervals <= 3 ft (<= 10 ft absolute) and at each end/joint
Vertical support detail at intervals <= 4 ft with no more than one joint between supports
Listing documentation where alternative support intervals are used

rules.title: Provide expansion fittings for thermal movement
rules.intent: Compensate for thermal expansion and contraction to prevent joint stress.
evidence_required: Expansion/contraction calculation for straight runs (per PVC characteristics, Table 352.44)
Location and type of expansion fittings on the wireway layout

rules.title: Keep splices accessible and within 75 percent fill
rules.intent: Ensure splices remain accessible and do not overfill the wireway.
evidence_required: Detail showing splice/tap locations accessible after installation
Fill calculation at splice points showing conductors + splices <= 75% of area

rules.title: Install separate equipment grounding conductor
rules.intent: Provide an effective ground-fault path since the nonmetallic raceway cannot serve as one.
evidence_required: One-line/cable schedule showing a separate equipment grounding conductor in the wireway
Documentation invoking 250.142 where grounded conductor is used for equipment grounding

rules.title: Ground extensions from nonmetallic wireway
rules.intent: Maintain grounding continuity through extensions made with Chapter 3 wiring methods.
evidence_required: Detail of extension wiring method (cord pendant or Chapter 3 method)
Equipment grounding conductor installed in or connection made to the extension wiring method

rules.title: Mark wireway with manufacturer and interior area
rules.intent: Ensure identification and fill information remains visible for inspection.
evidence_required: Product marking showing manufacturer name/trademark visible after installation
Marking showing interior cross-sectional area in square inches

rules.title: Limit multioutlet assembly to dry locations
rules.intent: Restrict multioutlet assemblies to dry locations for which they are suited.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming dry location for the assembly run

rules.title: Prohibit multioutlet assembly in unsuitable conditions
rules.intent: Prevent installation where concealment, damage, voltage, corrosion, or hazard conditions make the assembly unsafe.
evidence_required: Location/installation detail showing no concealment, hoistway, or corrosive vapor exposure
Metal thickness >= 0.040 in. where voltage between conductors is 300 V or more
Connection method confirming not cord-and-plug connected

rules.title: Apply deflection and pull-box dimensions to field-assembled multioutlet assemblies
rules.intent: Provide adequate bending and pull space for conductors in field-assembled multioutlet assemblies.
evidence_required: Dimension detail at deflection points meeting Table 312.6(A)
Pull distance calculation for 4 AWG and larger conductors per 314.28(A)(1)/(2)

rules.title: Allow metal multioutlet assembly through dry partitions with conditions
rules.intent: Permit pass-through of dry partitions only where covers are removable and no outlet is inside the partition.
evidence_required: Partition penetration detail showing assembly extends through (not within) the partition
Detail confirming caps/covers removable on exposed portions and no outlets inside the partition

rules.title: Limit nonmetallic extensions to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict nonmetallic extensions to existing 15/20A circuits, exposed dry locations, and low-rise residential/office occupancies.
evidence_required: Branch circuit documentation showing origin from existing 15A or 20A outlet
Occupancy classification (residential/office) and floor count <= 3 abovegrade, or identification for higher floors
Location detail confirming dry location and exposed/permitted-concealed routing

rules.title: Prohibit nonmetallic extensions in unsuitable locations
rules.intent: Prevent use in unfinished spaces, over voltage limits, in corrosive vapors, or beyond the originating room.
evidence_required: Routing detail confirming extension stays within the originating room and does not pass through floors/partitions
Circuit voltage documentation (<= 150 V surface / <= 300 V aerial)
Location classification confirming finished space and no corrosive vapors

rules.title: Keep surface extensions off the floor and conceal only where identified
rules.intent: Protect surface extensions from floor-level damage and limit concealment to identified products.
evidence_required: Mounting detail showing extension not on floor and at least 2 in. above floor
Product identification for concealment where extension is concealed with paint/plaster/etc.

rules.title: Secure nonmetallic surface extensions at required intervals
rules.intent: Ensure extensions are anchored and isolated from conductive materials.
evidence_required: Fastening layout showing intervals <= 8 in. (12 in. allowance to first fastening at attachment plug)
At least one fastening between each pair of adjacent outlets
Mounting detail confirming attachment only to woodwork/plaster and no contact with metalwork

rules.title: Use identified devices with concealable nonmetallic extensions
rules.intent: Ensure receptacles and self-contained devices are identified for and compatible with concealable extensions.
evidence_required: Device listing/identification marks for use with concealable nonmetallic extensions
Receptacle compliance documentation per 406.4

rules.title: Require continuous unspliced extension runs with covered taps
rules.intent: Prevent exposed conductors and unprotected splices in nonmetallic extensions.
evidence_required: Detail showing continuous unbroken assembly without splices between fittings
Approved tap fittings fully covering tap connections
Locking/polarized tap connector specification for aerial/receptacle-type taps

rules.title: Construct concealable extensions as layered flat conductor design
rules.intent: Ensure concealable extensions provide a sectioned grounded and equipment grounding conductor enclosing the ungrounded conductor.
evidence_required: Product cross-section/construction documentation showing multilayer flat conductor design
Listing confirming sectioned grounded and equipment grounding layers

rules.title: Use 14 or 12 AWG flat copper conductors with proper identification
rules.intent: Specify conductor sizes and identification for concealable extension construction.
evidence_required: Conductor specification confirming flat copper equivalent to 14 or 12 AWG
Conductor identification markings for ungrounded, grounded, and equipment grounding layers

rules.title: Insulate flat conductor layers
rules.intent: Ensure each conductor layer is properly insulated and the EGC covered or insulated.
evidence_required: Insulation specification for ungrounded and grounded flat conductor layers per 310.14(A)(3)
Confirmation equipment grounding conductor is covered or insulated

rules.title: Limit strut-type channel raceway to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict strut-type channel raceway to exposed, dry, and identified-protected conditions.
evidence_required: Location/exposure detail confirming exposed and dry (or approved-finish corrosive) use
Wall/floor pass-through detail with removable closure strips and covered portion within the assembly
Indoor-only confirmation where ferrous channel is enamel-protected only

rules.title: Prohibit strut-type channel raceway where concealed or severely corroded
rules.intent: Prevent concealment and unsuitable corrosion exposure of strut-type channel raceways.
evidence_required: Installation detail confirming raceway is not concealed
Corrosion environment assessment for ferrous enamel-protected channel

rules.title: Limit number of conductors by percentage fill
rules.intent: Limit conductor fill of strut-type channel raceway per Table 384.22 to prevent overheating.
evidence_required: Conductor fill calculation against Table 384.22 percentage fill for the channel size
Cross-sectional area references from Chapter 9 tables
Documentation supporting non-application of 310.15(C)(1) adjustment factors where claimed

rules.title: Secure and support strut-type channel raceway
rules.intent: Ensure raceway is mechanically supported at required intervals and near terminations.
evidence_required: Support layout showing intervals <= 10 ft and within 3 ft of each box/cabinet/termination
Retention strap detail for surface-mount runs or identified method for suspension mounts

rules.title: Provide grounding means at strut-type channel transitions
rules.intent: Ensure equipment grounding continuity at transitions and proper use as an EGC.
evidence_required: Detail of equipment grounding connection means at transitions to other wiring methods
Documentation where channel raceway is used as an EGC per 250.118(13)
Confirmation snap-fit covers are not relied on for receptacle EGC continuity

rules.title: Construct strut-type channel raceway of approved materials
rules.intent: Ensure raceways are formed of approved corrosion-protected materials and couple without abrasion.
evidence_required: Material specification (steel/stainless/aluminum) and corrosion protection method for steel
Construction documentation showing sections couple without subjecting wires to abrasion

rules.title: Limit surface metal raceway to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict surface metal raceway to dry locations and specifically permitted special conditions.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming dry location use
Pass-through detail showing unbroken length and conductor access on both sides
Documentation for special uses (Class I Div 2 or raised-floor)

rules.title: Prohibit surface metal raceway in unsuitable conditions
rules.intent: Prevent use where damage, voltage/thickness, corrosion, hoistway, or concealment conditions are unsafe.
evidence_required: Metal thickness >= 0.040 in. where voltage between conductors is 300 V or more
Location detail confirming no concealment, hoistway, or corrosive vapor exposure

rules.title: Limit conductors to raceway design number
rules.intent: Prevent overfill by limiting conductor count to the raceway's designed number.
evidence_required: Raceway design/listing showing maximum number of conductors
Conductor schedule confirming count within designed number
Documentation supporting non-application of 310.15(C)(1) where claimed

rules.title: Support surface metal raceway per manufacturer instructions
rules.intent: Ensure raceway support follows the listed installation instructions.
evidence_required: Manufacturer installation instructions showing support requirements
Support layout consistent with manufacturer instructions

rules.title: Limit splices and taps in surface metal raceway
rules.intent: Ensure accessible covers and 75 percent fill limit at splice points, or splice in boxes.
evidence_required: Detail showing removable cover accessible after installation at splice locations
Fill calculation at splice points <= 75% of area
Box detail where raceway lacks removable cover

rules.title: Provide grounding means at surface metal raceway transitions
rules.intent: Ensure equipment grounding continuity at transitions from other wiring methods.
evidence_required: Detail of equipment grounding connection means at raceway transitions

rules.title: Separate systems in combination raceways
rules.intent: Keep signaling and power/lighting circuits in separate identified compartments.
evidence_required: Raceway detail showing separate compartments for signaling vs power/lighting
Compartment identification method (stamping/imprinting/color coding)

rules.title: Limit surface nonmetallic raceway to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict surface nonmetallic raceway to dry locations and unbroken dry pass-throughs.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming dry location use
Pass-through detail showing unbroken length and conductor access on both sides

rules.title: Prohibit surface nonmetallic raceway in unsuitable conditions
rules.intent: Prevent use where concealment, damage, voltage, hoistway, hazard, or temperature conditions exceed the listing.
evidence_required: Location detail confirming no concealment, hoistway, or hazardous area
Listing voltage rating where voltage between conductors is 300 V or more
Conductor insulation and ambient temperature vs raceway listed ratings

rules.title: Limit splices and taps in surface nonmetallic raceway
rules.intent: Ensure openable accessible covers and 75 percent fill limit at splices, or splice in boxes.
evidence_required: Detail showing cover capable of being opened in place and accessible after installation
Fill calculation at splice points <= 75% of area
Box detail where raceway lacks openable cover

rules.title: Install separate EGC in surface nonmetallic raceway
rules.intent: Provide a ground-fault path since the nonmetallic raceway cannot serve as one.
evidence_required: One-line/cable schedule showing separate equipment grounding conductor in the raceway

rules.title: Limit underfloor raceway to permitted installations
rules.intent: Restrict underfloor raceways to beneath flooring or flush in office occupancies with floor covering.
evidence_required: Floor section detail showing raceway beneath flooring or flush per office occupancy
Floor covering specification (linoleum or equivalent) for flush installs

rules.title: Prohibit underfloor raceway in corrosive or hazardous conditions
rules.intent: Prevent installation in corrosive vapors and hazardous locations and protect metal raceways in corrosive concrete.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming no corrosive vapors or hazardous area
Corrosion protection / approved material documentation for metal raceways in concrete

rules.title: Provide required concrete cover over underfloor raceways
rules.intent: Maintain minimum cover depth over raceways for mechanical protection.
evidence_required: Floor section detail showing concrete/wood cover depth over each raceway width class
Raceway width and spacing dimensions on the plan

rules.title: Limit underfloor raceway fill to 40 percent
rules.intent: Prevent overheating by limiting conductor fill to 40 percent of interior area.
evidence_required: Conductor fill calculation showing combined area <= 40% of interior cross-sectional area
Raceway interior cross-sectional area documentation

rules.title: Make splices and taps only in junction boxes
rules.intent: Confine splices to junction boxes to maintain accessibility and integrity.
evidence_required: Junction box layout showing all splice/tap locations within boxes
Trench-type flush raceway detail with removable cover and <= 75% fill where exception is used

rules.title: Lay underfloor raceways in straight lines
rules.intent: Maintain raceway alignment between junction boxes for reliable conductor pulling.
evidence_required: Plan showing straight-line raceway runs coinciding with junction box centerlines
Detail showing raceways firmly held during construction

rules.title: Level and seal junction boxes; maintain metal continuity
rules.intent: Prevent water/concrete entry and maintain electrical continuity with metal raceways.
evidence_required: Junction box detail showing leveling to floor grade and sealing against water/concrete
Confirmation boxes used with metal raceways are metal and electrically continuous

rules.title: Level, seal, and secure inserts
rules.intent: Prevent concrete entry and maintain continuity and conductor protection at inserts.
evidence_required: Insert detail showing leveling and sealing against concrete entry
Confirmation inserts used with metal raceways are metal and electrically continuous
Method preventing chips/dirt from entering raceway during insert setting

rules.title: Use cable tray only for permitted wiring methods
rules.intent: Restrict cable tray contents to permitted wiring methods and require sunlight-resistant cables where sun-exposed.
evidence_required: Cable/raceway schedule confirming only Table 392.10(A) wiring methods are in the tray
Sunlight-resistance marking for cables exposed to direct sun
Listing/identification of trays and fittings for the intended use

rules.title: Prohibit cable tray in hoistways or where damaged
rules.intent: Prevent cable tray use where physical damage or hoistway conditions are unsafe.
evidence_required: Location detail confirming tray is not in a hoistway and not subject to severe physical damage

rules.title: Install cable tray as complete, accessible system
rules.intent: Ensure continuity, completion before cabling, exposure/accessibility, and proper marking of high-voltage trays.
evidence_required: Tray installation detail showing complete system with maintained electrical continuity and support
Confirmation each run is completed before cables are installed
Over-600 V warning notices placed at intervals not exceeding 10 ft where applicable
Wall/floor penetration detail per 300.21

rules.title: Separate over-1000V cables and group parallel conductors
rules.intent: Prevent unsafe mixing of voltage classes and current imbalance in paralleled single conductors.
evidence_required: Cable schedule showing over-1000 V cables are Type MC or separated by a solid fixed barrier
Parallel conductor grouping detail (one per phase/neutral/grounded per group)
Single-layer arrangement detail for 1/0 through 4/0 AWG single conductors

rules.title: Limit number/fill of cables in cable tray
rules.intent: Prevent overfill and overheating by limiting cable fill per tray type and conductor size.
evidence_required: Cable fill calculation per the applicable Table 392.22 column for tray type and cable size
Single-layer arrangement detail for 4/0 AWG and larger cables
Per-section fill calculation where dividers are used

rules.title: Secure and support cable trays, cables, and conductors
rules.intent: Ensure trays and their contents are supported per instructions and transitions are protected.
evidence_required: Tray support layout per manufacturer installation instructions
Detail showing cables fastened to transverse members in non-horizontal runs
Transition detail showing distance to raceway/equipment not exceeding 6 ft with conductors secured and protected

rules.title: Provide expansion splice plates where needed
rules.intent: Compensate for thermal expansion and contraction in cable tray runs.
evidence_required: Thermal expansion assessment for tray runs
Location of expansion splice plates on the tray layout

rules.title: Protect and seal bushed conduit/tubing transitions
rules.intent: Protect conductors transitioning from tray and prevent debris entering equipment.
evidence_required: Transition detail showing conductors secured at the tray and bushed conduit/tubing sealed at outer end
Detail confirming conductors are protected from abrasion at flanged or bushed openings

rules.title: Keep cable splices accessible in tray
rules.intent: Ensure splices are made by approved methods and remain accessible and protected.
evidence_required: Detail showing splices made/insulated by approved methods and accessible within the tray
Confirmation any splices projecting above side rails are not subject to physical damage

rules.title: Ground and bond metal cable trays
rules.intent: Ensure metal cable trays are grounded/bonded and meet criteria when used as an EGC.
evidence_required: Grounding/bonding detail for metal trays supporting conductors per 250.96 and Article 250 Part IV
Tray cross-sectional metal area and identification where used as an EGC (Table 392.60(B))
Bonding jumper detail (sized per 250.102) at mechanically discontinuous transitions

rules.title: Determine conductor ampacity per cable tray rules
rules.intent: Apply the correct ampacity tables and derating for cables installed in cable trays.
evidence_required: Ampacity calculation citing the applicable Table 310.16/310.17/310.18/310.19 values
Derating worksheet for covered trays (95%/70%/60% as applicable) and single-layer spacing
Identification of current-carrying conductor counts for adjustment factor application

rules.title: Construct cable trays with adequate strength and smooth edges
rules.intent: Ensure trays support wiring without damaging insulation and resist corrosion.
evidence_required: Tray construction/listing showing strength, rigidity, and smooth edges
Corrosion protection documentation for ferrous trays per 300.6
Flame-retardant material confirmation for nonmetallic trays

rules.title: Limit low-voltage suspended ceiling systems to permitted uses
rules.intent: Restrict these systems to listed Class 2 equipment, indoor dry locations, and qualifying occupancies.
evidence_required: Listing documentation for utilization equipment rated <= 30 V ac / 60 V dc at Class 2 power levels
Location classification confirming indoor dry location
Listing for use in environmental air space where applicable

rules.title: Prohibit suspended ceiling systems in unsuitable locations
rules.intent: Prevent use in damp/wet, corrosive, concealed, hazardous, fire-rated, and critical-care locations.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming indoor dry, accessible, non-hazardous location
Confirmation system is not part of a fire-rated assembly unless specifically listed
Confirmation not used for lighting in general or critical patient care areas

rules.title: Provide accessible in-sight disconnecting means
rules.intent: Ensure the Class 2 supply can be safely disconnected within sight for servicing.
evidence_required: Disconnecting means location detail showing accessibility and within sight of the Class 2 source
Confirmation simultaneous disconnection of all supply conductors on multiwire branch circuits

rules.title: Secure suspended ceiling system to building structure
rules.intent: Ensure the system and its power grid rails are mechanically secured to the structure.
evidence_required: Mounting detail showing attachment to building structure per installation instructions
Detail showing power grid rails mechanically secured to the overall ceiling grid assembly

rules.title: Use listed accessible connectors and enclosed wall connections
rules.intent: Ensure connections are listed, mechanically secure, accessible, and enclosed where in walls.
evidence_required: Connector listing documentation for busbar/cable/conductor connections
Detail showing connections accessible after installation
Enclosure detail per Article 314 for connections made in a wall

rules.title: Protect against overcurrent and reverse polarity
rules.intent: Limit overcurrent to 20 A and prevent unsafe interconnection or backfeed of Class 2 sources.
evidence_required: Overcurrent device rating documentation showing protection at not greater than 20 A
Listing documentation where Class 2 source outputs are interconnected/paralleled
Reverse polarity/backfeed protection detail for dc circuits

rules.title: Ground supply side and isolate load side of Class 2 source
rules.intent: Ensure proper grounding of the supply side and that load-side Class 2 circuits remain ungrounded.
evidence_required: Grounding detail showing supply side of Class 2 source connected to an EGC per Article 250 Part IV
Confirmation Class 2 load-side circuits are not grounded

rules.title: Specify minimum conductor sizes and types
rules.intent: Ensure load-side and power-feed conductors meet minimum copper sizes.
evidence_required: Conductor schedule showing load-side conductors are copper, 18 AWG minimum
Power feed bus rail specification (16 AWG minimum or equivalent)
Documentation for any 24-18 AWG Class 2 conductors per the exception

rules.title: Limit knob-and-tube to extensions or special permission
rules.intent: Restrict concealed knob-and-tube to existing extensions or special permission in permitted spaces.
evidence_required: Documentation that work is an extension of an existing installation, or special permission record
Location detail confirming installation in permitted hollow spaces or per 394.23 attics

rules.title: Prohibit knob-and-tube in hazardous or insulated spaces (California HCD amendment)
rules.intent: Prevent knob-and-tube in commercial garages, theaters, studios, hazardous locations, and insulation-enveloped spaces, with a California survey/certification path for added insulation.
evidence_required: Location classification confirming none of the prohibited occupancies/locations
CA-licensed electrical contractor survey/certification form filed with AHJ (HCD exception)
Bilingual caution notices posted in accessible insulated areas and noncombustible insulation documentation

rules.title: Protect knob-and-tube conductors through framing members
rules.intent: Protect conductors passing through framing with insulating tubes.
evidence_required: Detail showing insulating tubes/bushings where conductors pass through framing per 398.17
Detail confirming tubes extend at least 3 in. beyond wood cross members in plastered partitions

rules.title: Maintain knob-and-tube conductor clearances
rules.intent: Maintain separation between conductors and from surfaces and other materials.
evidence_required: Detail showing at least 3 in. between conductors and 1 in. to the surface
Detail showing flexible nonmetallic tubing where space is too limited (meters, panelboards, switch points)

rules.title: Protect knob-and-tube conductors in accessible attics
rules.intent: Protect attic conductors with running boards where they could be damaged.
evidence_required: Attic wiring detail showing running boards (1 in. each side) where conductors run through bored holes below 7 ft
Confirmation of attic accessibility (stairway/permanent ladder) and headroom for exception applicability

rules.title: Rigidly support knob-and-tube conductors
rules.intent: Support conductors on insulating materials at required intervals and near splices.
evidence_required: Support layout showing conductors on insulating supports within 6 in. of each tap/splice and at <= 4.5 ft intervals
Detail of flexible nonmetallic tubing where conductors are fished in dry locations

rules.title: Install knob-and-tube switches per 404 rules
rules.intent: Ensure switches comply with switch installation requirements.
evidence_required: Switch installation detail demonstrating compliance with 404.4 and 404.10(B)

rules.title: Solder knob-and-tube splices; prohibit in-line splices
rules.intent: Ensure mechanically and electrically sound splices in knob-and-tube wiring.
evidence_required: Splice detail showing soldered connections or approved splicing devices
Confirmation no in-line or strain splices are used

rules.title: Limit messenger-supported wiring to permitted cable types
rules.intent: Restrict messenger-supported wiring to Table 396.10(A) cable types and require weather/sunlight-rated conductors where exposed.
evidence_required: Cable schedule confirming only Table 396.10(A) cable types are used
Wet-location listing for conductors exposed to weather
Sunlight-resistance marking for sun-exposed conductors/cables

rules.title: Prohibit messenger-supported wiring in hoistways or where damaged
rules.intent: Prevent use where physical damage or hoistway conditions are unsafe.
evidence_required: Location detail confirming wiring is not in a hoistway and not subject to physical damage

rules.title: Support messenger to eliminate conductor tension
rules.intent: Ensure the messenger carries the load and conductors do not contact supports or structure.
evidence_required: Support detail showing messenger supported at dead ends and intermediate locations with no conductor tension
Detail confirming conductors do not contact messenger supports, structural members, walls, or pipes
Documentation where messenger serves as neutral or EGC (compliance with cited grounding sections)

rules.title: Ground the messenger
rules.intent: Ensure the messenger is grounded as required for enclosure grounding.
evidence_required: Grounding detail showing the messenger grounded per 250.80 and 250.86

rules.title: Limit open wiring to industrial/agricultural 1000V systems
rules.intent: Restrict open wiring on insulators to industrial/agricultural establishments on systems of 1000 V or less.
evidence_required: Occupancy classification confirming industrial or agricultural establishment
System voltage documentation confirming 1000 V nominal or less

rules.title: Prohibit concealed open wiring
rules.intent: Prevent open wiring on insulators from being concealed by building structure.
evidence_required: Installation detail confirming open wiring is not concealed by the building structure

rules.title: Protect exposed open conductors from physical damage
rules.intent: Protect conductors within 7 ft of the floor and where crossing framing from physical damage.
evidence_required: Detail of physical-damage protection (guard strips/running board/boxing/conduit) for conductors crossing framing or within 7 ft of floor
Detail of drip loops where conductors enter damp/wet/corrosive locations
Flexible nonmetallic tubing detail (<= 15 ft lengths, straps <= 4.5 ft) in dry locations

rules.title: Separate open conductors through framing members
rules.intent: Keep conductors out of contact with framing using individual insulating tubes/bushings.
evidence_required: Detail showing each conductor passing through a separate noncombustible insulating tube/sleeve
Detail of waterproof sleeve with insulating bushings where bushing is shorter than hole

rules.title: Maintain open conductor clearances from other materials
rules.intent: Maintain separation of open conductors from raceways, piping, and other conductors.
evidence_required: Clearance detail showing at least 2 in. separation from metal raceways/piping/other conductors, or a fixed nonconductor barrier
Routing detail showing conductors passing over piping subject to leakage where practicable

rules.title: Protect open conductors in accessible attics
rules.intent: Protect attic open conductors with running boards where they could be damaged.
evidence_required: Attic wiring detail showing running boards (1 in. each side) where conductors run through bored holes below 7 ft
Confirmation of attic accessibility and headroom for exception applicability

rules.title: Support open conductors by size at required intervals
rules.intent: Rigidly support open conductors on insulating materials at size-dependent intervals.
evidence_required: Support layout by conductor size (smaller than 8 AWG: within 6 in. of splice, 12 in. of dead-end, <= 4.5 ft intervals)
Detail for 8 AWG and larger across open spaces (<= 15 ft with spacers every 4.5 ft, >= 2.5 in. separation)
Support mounting hardware detail (nails/screws/cushion washers) per 398.30(D)

rules.title: Limit outdoor overhead conductors to over-1000V outdoor systems
rules.intent: Restrict outdoor overhead conductors to systems rated over 1000 V installed outdoors in free air.
evidence_required: System rating documentation confirming over 1000 V nominal
Installation detail confirming outdoor free-air routing

rules.title: Provide engineered support documentation for overhead conductors
rules.intent: Ensure conductor spacing, support structures, and insulators are engineered and documented for the loading and voltage.
evidence_required: Licensed professional engineer documentation of conductor spacing considering voltage, conductor size, span, structure type, and wind/ice loading
Engineered design of each support structure (soil, foundations, loading, guying, hardware) available to the AHJ
Insulator ratings for phase-to-phase voltage, mechanical strength, and impulse withstand BIL per Table 490.24

rules.title: Use connectors identified for the conductor material
rules.intent: Prevent overheating and failure of terminations caused by dissimilar-metal contact or unsuitable connection devices.
evidence_required: Conductor material callouts (Cu/Al) on plans and panel schedules
Connector/lug catalog cuts showing AL/CU or CU-only identification
Listing labels for splicing devices on fine-stranded conductors

rules.title: Coordinate conductor ampacity with termination temperature ratings
rules.intent: Ensure the conductor ampacity used in sizing never exceeds what the lowest-rated termination can safely carry.
evidence_required: Conductor schedule showing insulation type and ampacity column used (60C/75C)
Equipment termination temperature markings or listing data
Feeder/branch-circuit sizing calculations referencing Table 310.16

rules.title: Provide permanent lockable-open provisions on required lockable disconnects
rules.intent: Guarantee that a disconnecting means required to be lockable open can be secured for safe servicing at all times.
evidence_required: Disconnect schedule identifying lockable-open devices
Manufacturer cut sheets showing permanent locking provisions
One-line diagram locating each remote or lockable disconnect

rules.title: Provide and maintain working space about electrical equipment
rules.intent: Preserve safe access for operation and maintenance of energized equipment, including battery systems.
evidence_required: Equipment room plans with dimensioned working clearances
Elevation views showing 2.0 m headroom and dedicated space
Battery room layout showing clearance from rack/cabinet edges

rules.title: Guard live parts operating at 50 to 1000 volts against accidental contact
rules.intent: Prevent shock and arc injury from exposed live parts, including battery system live parts required to comply with 110.27.
evidence_required: Enclosure or barrier details for exposed live parts
Room access control notes limiting entry to qualified persons
Warning sign schedule per 110.21(B)

rules.title: Provide branch circuits sufficient for the calculated load
rules.intent: Ensure the branch-circuit count and ratings can serve the loads computed under Article 220.
evidence_required: Panel schedules with per-circuit connected loads
Article 220 load calculation summary
Floor plans keyed to branch-circuit numbers

rules.title: Scope: required dedicated branch circuits in dwelling units
rules.intent: Trigger the dwelling-unit dedicated circuit requirements of 210.11(C)(1) through (C)(4).
evidence_required: Panel schedule identifying small-appliance, laundry, bathroom, and garage circuits
Dwelling unit floor plan with receptacle circuiting

rules.title: Provide two or more 20-ampere small-appliance branch circuits
rules.intent: Reserve adequate capacity for kitchen and dining small-appliance receptacle loads in dwellings.
evidence_required: Panel schedule showing two or more 20 A small-appliance circuits
Kitchen/dining receptacle circuiting on floor plans

rules.title: Provide a dedicated 20-ampere garage branch circuit
rules.intent: Ensure garage receptacles in dwellings have dedicated capacity for typical equipment loads.
evidence_required: Panel schedule showing dedicated garage circuit
Garage receptacle layout per 210.52(G)(1)

rules.title: Scope: branch-circuit conductor minimum ampacity and size
rules.intent: Route branch-circuit conductor sizing to the applicable subsection based on circuit voltage and load type.
evidence_required: Branch-circuit conductor schedule

rules.title: Restrict wiring in ducts, plenums, and other air-handling spaces to methods complying with 300.22

Wiring method and cable listing documentation for plenum spaces
Support-accessory (cable tie) listing data for plenum installations

Raceway fill calculations for each IMC run

Site plan confirming no FMC in underground or embedded runs

rules.title: Limit FMC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4, with 3/8 permitted only for listed short applications

Details for any 3/8 trade size FMC showing qualifying application and length limit
Luminaire tap connection details

Ceiling-space luminaire whip details where exceptions apply

Details for any 3/8 LFMC showing qualifying 348.20(A) application

rules.title: Use PVC conduit only in the locations permitted by 352.10(A) through (I)

Schedule 80 or identified PVC specification where exposed to physical damage

rules.title: Limit PVC conduit to trade sizes 1/2 through 6

Raceway fill calculations for PVC runs

rules.title: Limit HDPE conduit to trade sizes 1/2 through 6

Underground duct bank details for HDPE runs

rules.title: Mark NUCC every 10 ft per 110.21 and identify enclosed conductors per 310.8

Assembly end/reel tag identifying enclosed conductors
Field verification photos of installed markings

rules.title: Limit NUCC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4
rules.intent: Keep nonmetallic underground conduit with conductors within manufactured/listed size range.

Bending radius verification per Table 354.24

rules.title: Limit RTRC to trade sizes 1/2 through 6

RTRC listing data (e.g., Type XW where exposed to damage)

rules.title: Mark LFNC every 2 ft with type designation and trade size per 110.21

Direct burial/outdoor marking verification
Prewired assembly tag detail

rules.title: Scope: LFNC type designations (LFNC-A, LFNC-B, LFNC-C)

Elevator/escalator details where LFNC-B lengths over 6 ft rely on 356.2(2)

rules.title: Limit LFNC to trade sizes 1/2 through 4, with 3/8 only for motor leads or short luminaire/equipment taps

Details for 3/8 LFNC applications with length verification

rules.title: Limit FMT to trade sizes 1/2 through 3/4, with 3/8 only per 300.22(B)/(C) or short luminaire assemblies

Luminaire whip length verification for 3/8 FMT

rules.title: Limit ENT to trade sizes 1/2 through 2 1/2

Building height/thermal barrier documentation supporting ENT use per 362.10

rules.title: Identify grounded fixture wire per 402.8

Fixture wire specifications (type and identification means)

rules.title: Limit luminaire tap connections in small flexible raceways to 6 ft per 410.117(C)

Listed assembly documentation for prefabricated luminaire whips

rules.title: Scope: auxiliary equipment limitations for electric-discharge and LED lamps per 410.137

Branch-circuit voltage documentation per 210.6

rules.intent: Screw shell lampholders on circuits with a grounded conductor must have the screw shell connected to the grounded conductor, protecting persons relamping.

Lampholder terminal identification per 200.10(C)

rules.intent: Appliances identified in 422.5(A) must have GFCI protection from either the appliance side (422.5(B)(3)-(B)(5)) or the outlet/branch-circuit side (422.5(B)(1) or (B)(2)).

Panel schedule or device schedule showing GFCI protection for those outlets
Appliance listing data where appliance-integral GFCI (422.5(B)(3)-(B)(5)) is relied upon

rules.title: Scope: appliances specified in 422.5(A) trigger GFCI requirements
rules.intent: The 422.5(A) appliance list (including vending machines per (A)(5) and dishwashers) defines which appliance outlets require GFCI protection.

GFCI protection mapping for each flagged appliance outlet

rules.title: GFCI-protect branch circuits supplying vending machines
rules.intent: Vending machines without appliance-integral GFCI must be supplied from GFCI-protected branch circuits.

Panel schedule showing GFCI protection on vending machine branch circuits
Vending machine listing data if integral GFCI is claimed

rules.title: Scope: 422.5(B)(1) is an accepted supply-side GFCI means for appliance outlets

Panel schedule cross-reference for the protected appliance circuit

rules.title: Scope: appliance-side GFCI per 422.5(B)(3) relieves the outlet GFCI requirement

rules.title: Apply 426.28 equipment ground-fault protection to dedicated de-icing/snow-melting receptacle circuits in lieu of GFCI

GFPE device specification per 426.28

rules.title: Scope: undersized raceway permitted only for enclosing motor leads per 430.245(B)

Motor equipment submittal identifying factory lead arrangement

rules.title: Provide grounding-type, GFCI-protected receptacle outlets in mobile and manufactured homes

Manufacturer wiring diagram showing grounding-type devices
Dielectric/continuity/polarity test records per 550.17

rules.title: Scope: GFCI requirements for boat hoists per 555.9
rules.intent: Flag that boat hoist outlets have dedicated GFCI requirements in Article 555 beyond the general 210.8 provisions.

GFCI device schedule for boat hoist outlets

rules.title: Use listed portable-type GFCI protection for cord-and-plug-connected temporary wiring
rules.intent: Temporary wiring GFCI protection supplied through plug-and-cord connection must be listed portable GFCI or equivalent so protection travels with the connection.
evidence_required: Temporary power plan identifying GFCI means for each circuit
Listing data for portable GFCI cord sets or devices
Assured equipment grounding conductor program documentation where used

rules.title: Restrict manufactured wiring systems to accessible dry locations and listed air-handling applications
rules.intent: Manufactured wiring systems are limited to accessible, dry locations unless listed for ducts/plenums and installed per 300.22, or listed for outdoor use.
evidence_required: Manufactured wiring system listing documentation
Reflected ceiling plan showing accessible installation locations
Plenum listing evidence where installed in air-handling spaces

rules.title: Use specified raceway or metal-clad cable wiring methods in elevator hoistways, machine rooms, and cars
rules.intent: Confine elevator, escalator, and lift wiring to robust raceway/cable methods, with flexible methods limited to 6 ft lengths except as specifically excepted.
evidence_required: Elevator electrical plans showing wiring methods in hoistway, car, and machine room
Details of flexible conduit lengths (6 ft limit) at controllers and machines
Class 2 cable support and protection details in hoistways
For OSHPD 1 projects, seismic switch hardwiring detail

rules.title: Supply other elevator utilization equipment from additional branch circuits with OCPDs in the machine/control room
rules.intent: Keep utilization equipment beyond car lighting, machine-room, and pit circuits on separate branch circuits with overcurrent devices located where elevator personnel can find them.
evidence_required: Elevator power riser/one-line showing separate branch circuits for other utilization equipment
Panel schedule locating overcurrent devices in machine/control room
Equipment list confirming loads fall within 620.1 scope

rules.title: Provide 110.26(A) working clearances at elevator controllers and disconnecting means

Documentation of any 620.5(A)-(D) condition relied upon (flexible leads, guarding, low voltage)
Maintenance/supervision statement where clearance relief is claimed

rules.title: Identify solidly grounded PV system conductors at terminations per 200.6(A)

PV cable specification (single-conductor, sunlight-resistant, outdoor-rated)

rules.title: Supply PLFA circuits from listed power sources on dedicated, identified branch circuits without GFCI/AFCI
rules.intent: Power-limited fire alarm systems must have a listed power source and a dedicated, red-identified, qualified-access branch circuit that cannot be interrupted by GFCI or AFCI devices.

Panel schedule showing dedicated fire alarm branch circuit without GFCI/AFCI
Fire alarm control unit label identifying the branch-circuit OCPD location
Red-identified disconnect detail marked FIRE ALARM CIRCUIT

rules.title: Supply NPLFA circuits at 600 V or less from Chapters 1-4 compliant sources on dedicated, identified branch circuits without GFCI/AFCI
rules.intent: Non-power-limited fire alarm circuits need a code-compliant power source not over 600 volts and a dedicated, red-identified branch circuit immune to GFCI/AFCI interruption.

Panel schedule showing dedicated fire alarm branch circuit without GFCI/AFCI
Fire alarm control unit label identifying branch-circuit OCPD location
Red-identified disconnect detail marked FIRE ALARM CIRCUIT

rules.title: Provide compliant insulation and independent continuity for grounded conductors
rules.intent: Ensure the grounded (neutral) conductor is insulated equivalently to ungrounded conductors and remains continuous without relying on metallic enclosures, so the return path is never interrupted by hardware changes.
evidence_required: Conductor schedule or panel schedule showing grounded conductor insulation type and voltage rating
One-line diagram identifying system grounding (solidly grounded vs. impedance grounded) and system voltage
Wiring details showing grounded conductor spliced/terminated independent of enclosures, raceways, or cable armor

rules.title: Identify grounded-conductor terminals on devices, receptacles, plugs, and screw shells
rules.intent: Prevent reversed polarity by making the terminal intended for the grounded conductor visually identifiable on wiring devices.
evidence_required: Device and receptacle cut sheets showing white/silver grounded-terminal identification or 'W' marking
Fixture/lampholder details showing screw shell wired to the grounded conductor
Appliance listing documentation identifying the grounded circuit conductor terminal

rules.title: Install multiwire branch circuits with common origin, simultaneous disconnect, line-to-neutral loads, and grouping

Circuit directory/load list confirming line-to-neutral loads only
Wiring detail or note requiring grouping of multiwire circuit conductors in enclosures

rules.title: Provide ground-fault protection of equipment on large feeder disconnects

Voltage system documentation (e.g., 480Y/277 V) confirming applicability

rules.title: Size essential electrical system feeders per 215.2 and Article 220 Part III

Essential electrical system demand calculation and connected load summary

rules.title: Add a downstream level of ground-fault protection in health care facilities where service/feeder GFPE is provided

GFPE relay/CT specifications for the downstream level
Riser diagram showing GFPE devices located upstream of essential electrical system transfer switches

rules.title: Scope: 240.15(B) governs use of single-pole circuit breakers as multiwire disconnecting means

Manufacturer documentation for identified handle ties

rules.title: Bond electrode-type boiler metal parts per 250.102 with full-ampacity bonding jumper

Bonding jumper size calculation compared to neutral conductor ampacity
Grounded neutral conductor specification (insulated 1000 V minimum, run with ungrounded conductors)

Detail showing wire-type EGC where flexibility is required after installation

Cable listing documentation showing armor/sheath qualifies as an EGC per 250.118
Floor plans identifying patient care spaces served

rules.title: Size equipment grounding conductors and bonding jumpers per 250.122

Feeder bonding jumper sizes on one-line diagram
Specification requiring insulated copper EGCs in patient care spaces

Justification for any separately run EGC citing the applicable 250.134 exception

rules.title: Use the grounded circuit conductor to ground equipment only where 250.142 permits

rules.title: Rate insulated grounded conductors of solidly grounded systems over 1000 V at not less than 600 V

rules.title: Make equipment grounding conductor connections to busways and wireways per 250.8

Specification note invoking 300.13(B) for multiwire branch circuits

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in HDPE conduit

EGC size per Table 250.122 on circuit schedules
Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

rules.title: Use RTRC and fittings constructed of suitable resistant nonmetallic material

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in RTRC conduit
rules.intent: Provide a wire-type fault-current path because RTRC conduit is nonmetallic and cannot serve as an equipment grounding conductor.

Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

Current-limiting device rating documentation where exception used

rules.title: Protect flexible cords and fixture wires per 240.5

rules.title: Install luminaire-supporting outlet boxes as required by 314.23

Ceiling framing attachment details

Locking support and mounting receptacle product listing where used

Receptacle-outlet count calculation using 12 in. per outlet

rules.title: Mount receptacles in countertops and work surfaces per 406.5
rules.intent: Scope rule: receptacle mounting in countertops and work surfaces is governed by 406.5(E), (F), and (G); the source text in this community contains only the cross-reference, so this rule captures the trigger for that subtree.
evidence_required: Countertop/work-surface receptacle assembly product listings
Installation details referencing 406.5(E), (F), (G)

rules.title: Use listed countertop receptacle outlet assemblies in countertops
rules.intent: Permit receptacles in countertops only where the receptacle outlet assembly is listed for use in countertops.

Plan location of countertop-installed receptacles
Manufacturer installation instructions

rules.title: Use listed work-surface receptacle outlet assemblies in work surfaces

Plan location of work-surface-installed receptacles

rules.title: Comply with 406.5(G) for receptacles in countertops and work surfaces
rules.intent: Scope rule: 406.5(G) governs installation of receptacles in both countertops and work surfaces (referenced from 210.52(C)(3) and 210.52(D)); the source text in this community contains only the cross-reference.
evidence_required: Installation details for countertop/work-surface receptacles
Product listing documentation

rules.title: Keep suspended luminaires, track, pendants, and paddle fans out of the bathtub/shower zone
rules.intent: Prevent shock hazard by excluding cord-, chain-, or cable-suspended luminaires, lighting track, pendants, and ceiling-suspended (paddle) fans from the zone around bathtubs and showers, and by requiring damp/wet-location marking within the zone.

Luminaire schedule with damp/wet location markings
Fixture cut sheets showing suspension type

rules.title: Install lighting track permanently, within its rating, and outside prohibited locations
rules.intent: Ensure lighting track is permanently installed and connected, loaded within its rating, supplied by a branch circuit not exceeding the track rating, and kept out of prohibited locations.

Reflected ceiling plan showing track locations and mounting heights
Track and fitting listing documentation
Connected fixture load tabulation per track run

rules.title: Support luminaires by compliant outlet boxes or fittings
rules.intent: Ensure luminaires supported by outlet boxes use boxes installed per 314.23 that comply with 314.27, and recognize 314.27(E) boxes as required lighting outlets.
evidence_required: Box mounting and support details
Box listing showing luminaire support rating
Lighting plan cross-referencing required lighting outlets

rules.title: Meet cord-connection conditions for lampholders and luminaires
rules.intent: Ensure cord-connected lampholders and electric-discharge/LED luminaires are protected against cord damage and connected only under the permitted conditions.

Field condition photos or details showing cord routing and visibility
Branch-circuit rating versus luminaire full-load current calculation

rules.title: Support ceiling-suspended (paddle) fans by listed means
rules.intent: Prevent falling fans by requiring support independent of an outlet box or by listed fan-rated boxes/box systems per 314.27(C) or listed locking support and mounting receptacle systems per 314.27(E).
evidence_required: Fan-rated box listing labels or independent support details
Fan mounting installation instructions
Locking support and mounting receptacle listing where used

rules.title: Use listed locking support and mounting receptacles within their ratings
rules.intent: Allow appliances to be supported and connected by separable attachment fittings only where the locking support and mounting receptacle is listed, compatible, used within its ratings, and installed per 314.27(E).
evidence_required: Listing documentation for locking support and mounting receptacle
Appliance and fitting compatibility/rating data
Installation detail referencing 314.27(E)

rules.title: Wire strip lights and connector strips with 125 degree C insulated conductors at 60 degree C ampacity
rules.intent: Protect stage strip-light and connector-strip wiring from heat degradation by mandating high-temperature insulation while limiting ampacity to 60 degree C values.

Ampacity calculation using 60 degree C column
Connector strip shop drawings showing drop wire type and length

rules.title: Construct portable strips like border lights and protect their supply cables
rules.intent: Ensure portable strip lights meet border-light construction requirements and that supply cables are bushed and strain-relieved.
evidence_required: Portable strip construction/shop drawings or listing data
Bushing and strain-relief details at cable entries
Cable type documentation (extra-hard usage where required)

rules.title: Use listed extra-hard usage cords for portable stage equipment
rules.intent: Ensure flexible conductors supplying portable stage equipment are rated for the abuse of stage environments, with limited hard-usage allowances only under protected, 20-ampere-or-less conditions.
evidence_required: Cord/cable listing and usage designation (extra-hard vs hard usage)
Branch-circuit overcurrent device ratings for portable equipment circuits
Cord routing/support details for protected applications
Ampacity determination per 400.5 or Table 520.44(C)(2)

rules.title: Apply 210.8 branch-circuit outlet GFCI protection in addition to equipment-specific GFCI rules
rules.intent: Ensure that equipment-level GFCI requirements in Articles 422 and 424 are applied on top of, not instead of, the branch-circuit outlet GFCI protection required by 210.8 for covered locations.
evidence_required: Panel schedule identifying GFCI-protected branch circuits serving covered locations
Floor plan showing receptacle and equipment outlet locations relative to 210.8 covered areas (bathrooms, kitchens, etc.)
One-line or circuit diagram showing GFCI device placement for each covered outlet

rules.title: Provide listed GFCI protection for cord-connected horticultural lighting equipment
rules.intent: Protect personnel from ground faults on horticultural lighting equipment that uses flexible cords, which is commonly handled and used in damp growing environments.
evidence_required: Luminaire schedule identifying horticultural lighting equipment and its listing
Circuit/panel schedule showing GFCI protection on lighting outlets supplying the horticultural equipment
Cut sheets or listing labels for the GFCI device
Wiring plan showing flexible cord connections to the protected lighting outlets

rules.title: Classify lighting systems under Article 411 by voltage and wet-contact limits
rules.intent: Establish which lighting systems fall under the low-voltage lighting rules of Article 411 so the correct requirement subtree is applied.
evidence_required: Lighting system cut sheets showing operating voltage (ac/dc)
Plans identifying locations where wet contact is likely
Power supply/transformer specifications for the low-voltage system

rules.title: Install concealed or through-structure low-voltage lighting conductors by Chapter 3 methods or Class 2 wiring per 725.130
rules.intent: Ensure low-voltage lighting conductors hidden in building construction are installed with recognized wiring methods so they remain safe and inspectable.
evidence_required: Wiring plan showing routing of concealed low-voltage lighting conductors
Specification of the wiring method used (Chapter 3 method or Class 2 cable type)
Listing documentation for the Class 2 power source where option (2) is used

rules.title: Keep low-voltage lighting systems at least 10 ft horizontally from pool, spa, or fountain water
rules.intent: Prevent shock hazard from low-voltage lighting systems installed near bodies of water unless the stricter rules of Article 680 permit closer installation.
evidence_required: Site or floor plan dimensioning lighting system locations from the nearest water edge
Luminaire schedule identifying the low-voltage lighting system components
Article 680 compliance documentation where systems are closer than 10 ft

rules.title: Provide Class A GFCI protection for listed appliance categories rated 150 V or less to ground and 60 A or less
rules.intent: Protect personnel from electrocution by ground faults on appliance categories with elevated shock risk, using a readily accessible, listed Class A GFCI.
evidence_required: Appliance schedule with voltage-to-ground and ampere ratings for each covered appliance
Panel schedule or circuit diagram showing the Class A GFCI device and its location in the supply path
Listing labels or cut sheets for the GFCI device (or factory-installed appliance GFCI)
Plan notes demonstrating the GFCI is readily accessible

rules.title: Meet cord length, receptacle, and grounding conditions for cord-and-plug-connected in-sink waste disposers
rules.intent: Allow flexible-cord connection of in-sink waste disposers only when the cord and receptacle arrangement keeps the cord protected, accessible, and grounded.
evidence_required: Appliance cut sheet and manufacturer installation instructions identifying the suitable cord
Kitchen plan/detail showing receptacle location relative to the disposer
Cord specification showing length between 18 in. and 36 in. and equipment grounding conductor
Listing label documentation where double-insulation exception is claimed

rules.title: Meet cord length, receptacle location, and grounding conditions for built-in dishwashers and trash compactors
rules.intent: Allow flexible-cord connection of built-in dishwashers and trash compactors only when cord length, receptacle placement, and grounding keep the installation safe and serviceable.
evidence_required: Manufacturer installation instructions identifying the suitable flexible cord
Kitchen plan/detail showing receptacle located in the adjacent space (dishwasher) or occupied/adjacent space (compactor)
Cord specification showing length within 3-6.5 ft (dishwasher) or 3-4 ft (compactor) with equipment grounding conductor
Detail of bushing or grommet protection where the cord passes through an opening

rules.title: Identify oven/cooking-unit supply connectors for the temperature of the space
rules.intent: Ensure separable connectors or plug-and-receptacle combinations serving wall-mounted ovens and counter-mounted cooking units withstand the heat of their installed location.
evidence_required: Appliance installation instructions identifying cord/connector suitability
Cut sheet or listing label for the connector showing its temperature rating
Detail showing the connector location relative to the oven or cooking unit

rules.title: Meet cord, receptacle, and individual-branch-circuit conditions for range hoods and microwave/range hood combinations
rules.intent: Allow flexible-cord connection of range hoods and over-the-range microwave/hood combinations only when the cord is protected, grounded, and supplied by an accessible receptacle on an individual branch circuit.
evidence_required: Panel schedule showing the individual branch circuit dedicated to the range hood receptacle
Manufacturer installation instructions identifying the suitable cord for range hood use
Kitchen elevation/detail showing accessible receptacle placement protecting the cord
Cord specification showing length within 18 in. to 4 ft with equipment grounding conductor

rules.title: Secure, protect, and GFCI-protect heating cables installed in concrete or poured masonry floors
rules.intent: Prevent damage to embedded floor-heating cables and protect occupants of wet-prone rooms from ground faults in electrically heated floors.
evidence_required: Floor heating layout plan showing cable runs, securing method, and lead exit points
Conduit/raceway specification for leads leaving the floor (RMC, IMC, rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT)
Panel schedule showing GFCI protection on circuits serving heated floors in bathrooms, kitchens, and hydromassage tub locations
Manufacturer installation instructions for adjacent run spacing

rules.title: Identify, anchor, ground, and GFCI-protect heating cables installed under floor coverings
rules.intent: Ensure under-floor-covering heating cables are suitable for the application, mechanically secure, provided with a grounding path, and GFCI-protected against ground faults.
evidence_required: Cut sheet/listing showing the cable is identified for under-floor-covering installation
Panel schedule showing GFCI protection for personnel on the supplying branch circuit
Floor heating layout showing expansion joints and any expansion/contraction fittings
Product data showing integral grounding braid or metal sheath over the heated length

rules.title: Identify, anchor, ground, and GFCI-protect heating panels and panel sets installed under floor coverings
rules.intent: Ensure radiant heating panels and panel sets under floor coverings are suitable for the application, properly installed with recognized wiring methods, grounded, and GFCI-protected.
evidence_required: Listing documentation showing panels/panel sets identified for under-floor-covering installation
Panel schedule showing GFCI protection for personnel on branch circuits supplying the panels
Wiring plan showing Chapter 3 wiring method connections to branch-circuit and supply wiring
Manufacturer instructions and floor covering suitability identification
Product data showing integral grounding braid or metal sheath

rules.title: Install Class 2 supplied low-voltage lighting wiring in accordance with 725.130
rules.intent: Route the Class 2 wiring option for concealed low-voltage lighting conductors to the installation requirements of 725.130.
evidence_required: Listing documentation for the Class 2 power source
Wiring plan identifying the Class 2 circuit routing and cable type
Installation notes citing compliance with 725.130 wiring methods

rules.title: Provide and maintain access and working space about all electrical equipment
rules.intent: Ensure workers can operate and maintain electrical equipment readily and safely without obstruction.
evidence_required: Floor plans showing clear working space dimensions at each piece of electrical equipment
Equipment layout / electrical room plan with clearances dimensioned
Notes on plans prohibiting storage in required working space

rules.title: Provide dimensioned working space at equipment likely to be serviced while energized
rules.intent: Guarantee minimum working-space dimensions around equipment operating at 1000 volts or less that may be examined, adjusted, or serviced while energized.

requires.alternative: as required or permitted elsewhere in this Code

evidence_required: Electrical room and equipment layout plans with working space depth, width, and height dimensioned
Panel schedules and equipment schedules identifying nominal voltage to ground
Elevation details showing 90-degree door/hinged-panel opening clearance

rules.title: Maintain minimum working-space depth per Table 110.26(A)(1)
rules.intent: Keep enough clear depth in front of live parts for a worker to safely service energized equipment.

requires.measured_from: exposed live parts, or from the enclosure or opening if the live parts are enclosed

exceptions.note: Working space not required in back or sides; where rear access is required for nonelectrical parts, a minimum horizontal working space of 762 mm (30 in.) shall be provided.

evidence_required: Dimensioned plan showing depth of working space in the direction of live parts at each equipment location
Identification of working-space Condition (1, 2, or 3) for each equipment location (grounded walls, opposing live parts)
Equipment schedules with nominal voltage to ground
For Exception No. 3: written operating procedures and qualified-person maintenance documentation

rules.title: Provide egress at each end of working space for large equipment
rules.intent: Ensure workers can escape from the working space of large equipment during an electrical incident.
evidence_required: Electrical room floor plan showing entrance/egress locations and dimensions at each end of the working space
Equipment schedule or one-line diagram showing equipment ampere ratings and physical widths
Door swing details demonstrating open equipment doors do not impede egress
For single-entrance option: dimensioned plan demonstrating unobstructed egress or doubled working-space depth

rules.title: Locate switchboards, switchgear, panelboards, and motor control centers in dedicated spaces
rules.intent: Protect major distribution equipment from damage and preserve space for the electrical installation.
evidence_required: Floor plans showing dedicated space at each switchboard, switchgear, panelboard, and motor control center
Reflected ceiling and mechanical/plumbing coordination drawings showing no foreign systems in the dedicated zone
Details of physical protection where equipment is subject to damage

rules.title: Keep indoor dedicated electrical space clear of foreign systems
rules.intent: Reserve the zone above and around indoor distribution equipment for the electrical installation and prevent damage from foreign systems.

requires.dedicated_space_footprint: width and depth of the equipment
requires.dedicated_space_vertical_extent: floor to 1.8 m (6 ft) above the equipment or to the structural ceiling, whichever is lower
requires.foreign_systems_above_dedicated_space: permitted only where protection is installed to avoid damage from condensation, leaks, or breaks
requires.sprinkler_protection: permitted for the dedicated space where the piping complies with this section

evidence_required: Coordinated plan/section showing the dedicated zone from floor to 6 ft above equipment (or structural ceiling) free of foreign systems
Mechanical, plumbing, and fire sprinkler drawings overlaid at electrical equipment locations
Details of drip protection where foreign systems are located above the dedicated space

rules.title: Guard live parts against accidental contact, protect equipment from damage, and post warning signs
rules.intent: Prevent accidental contact with energized parts and warn unqualified persons away from exposed live parts.

guarded_by_approved_enclosures_or_one_of: location in a room, vault, or similar enclosure accessible only to qualified persons
permanent, substantial partitions or screens with openings sized/located to prevent accidental contact
location on a balcony, gallery, or platform elevated and arranged to exclude unqualified persons
elevation above floor: >= 2.5 m (8 ft) for 50-300 V; >= 2.6 m (8 ft 6 in.) for 301-600 V; >= 2.62 m (8 ft 7 in.) for 601-1000 V between ungrounded conductors
requires.physical_damage_protection: in locations where equipment is likely to be exposed to physical damage, enclosures or guards shall be arranged and of such strength as to prevent such damage
requires.warning_signs: entrances to rooms and other guarded locations containing exposed live parts shall be marked with conspicuous warning signs forbidding unqualified persons to enter, meeting 110.21(B)

evidence_required: Plans identifying rooms/vaults/enclosures restricting access to qualified persons
Details of partitions, screens, or elevation dimensions guarding exposed live parts
Enclosure or guard details at locations subject to physical damage
Warning sign schedule and mounting locations complying with 110.21(B)

rules.title: Install a service receptacle within 25 ft of equipment requiring servicing
rules.intent: Give service personnel a power source for tools and instruments near equipment they must maintain.

evidence_required: Power plan showing 125 V, 15- or 20-A receptacle within 25 ft of each HVAC/refrigeration unit and on the same level
Receptacle location within the same room or area as indoor service equipment and dedicated-space equipment
Panel schedule showing the service receptacle circuit is not fed from the load side of the equipment disconnecting means

rules.title: Install required lighting outlets, including at spaces containing equipment requiring servicing
rules.intent: Provide illumination for occupants and for personnel servicing equipment in dwellings, guest rooms, and utility spaces.

requires.dwelling_habitable_rooms: at least one lighting outlet controlled by a listed wall-mounted control device in every habitable room, kitchen, and bathroom; control device located near an entrance on a wall
requires.all_occupancies_storage_and_equipment_sp: at least one lighting outlet containing a switch or controlled by a wall switch or listed wall-mounted control device; a point of control at each entry; lighting outlet at or near equipment requiring servicing
requires.interior_stairways_six_or_more_risers: listed wall-mounted control device at each floor level and landing level that includes an entryway

evidence_required: Lighting plans showing lighting outlets and wall-mounted control devices in each required room and space
Lighting outlet shown at or near equipment requiring servicing in attics, underfloor spaces, utility rooms, and basements
Switching diagram for interior stairways with six or more risers showing control at each floor and landing level with entryway

rules.title: Apply Article 215 to feeder installation, overcurrent protection, sizing, and ampacity
rules.intent: Establish the scope of feeder requirements so plans for feeders are checked against Article 215.
evidence_required: One-line diagram identifying all feeders
Feeder schedule with conductor sizes, ampacities, and overcurrent protection
Identification of any electrolytic cell line feeders claimed under the 668.3(C) exception

rules.title: Apply 480.10(D) top clearance to battery systems on open racks
rules.intent: Route working-space height compliance for open-rack battery systems to the battery-specific top-clearance provision instead of the general 110.26(A)(3) height rule.

requires.note: Scope rule: Article 480 text is not contained in the source files for this community; this trigger is extracted from 110.26(A)(3) Exception No. 1, which defers open-rack battery top clearance to 480.10(D).

evidence_required: Battery system layout drawings showing rack type (open rack) and top clearance dimensions
Manufacturer installation instructions for the battery racks
Working space plan referencing 480.10(D) clearance at the battery installation

rules.title: Apply Chapters 1-4 to electrolytic cell lines except as amended by 668.3(C)
rules.intent: Define which general Code requirements (including Article 110 working space) apply, or are relaxed, within electrolytic cell line installations.

requires.chapters_1_through_4_apply_to: services, feeders, branch circuits, and apparatus supplying lighting, ventilating, material handling, and the like outside the electrolytic cell line working zone
requires.systems_not_electrically_connected_to_ce: shall comply with all applicable sections of this Code
cell_lines_comply_with_chapters_1_throug: 668.3(C)(1): cell line conductors not required to comply with Articles 110, 210, 215, 220, and 225 (see 668.12)
668.3(C)(2): overcurrent protection of electrolytic cell dc process power circuits not required to comply with Article 240
668.3(C)(3): equipment within the cell line working zone or associated with cell line dc power circuits not required to comply with Article 250 except as required by Article 668
668.3(C)(4): cells, cell line attachments, and wiring of auxiliary equipment within the working zone not required to comply with Articles 110, 210, 215, 220, and 225 (see 668.30)

evidence_required: Site plan delineating the electrolytic cell line working zone boundary
One-line diagram separating cell line dc process circuits from general lighting/ventilating/material-handling circuits
Documentation identifying which circuits claim the 668.3(C) exemptions from Articles 110/210/215/220/225/240/250

rules.title: Construct cell line conductors of suitable material, adequate size, and approved connections
rules.intent: Ensure cell line conductors, which are exempt from general conductor articles, are still safe under maximum load and ambient conditions.

requires.insulation_and_material: bare, covered, or insulated; copper, aluminum, copper-clad aluminum, steel, or other suitable material
requires.sizing_criterion: cross-sectional area such that temperature rise under maximum load conditions and at maximum ambient does not exceed the safe operating temperature of the conductor insulation or the material of the conductor supports
requires.connections: joined by bolted, welded, clamped, or compression connectors

evidence_required: Cell line conductor specifications (material, cross-sectional area, insulation/covering)
Temperature-rise calculation at maximum load and maximum ambient
Connection details showing bolted, welded, clamped, or compression connectors

rules.title: Ground required cell line equipment via a local grounding electrode system
rules.intent: Provide a compliant grounding electrode system for cell line equipment that Article 668 requires to be grounded.

requires.grounding_per: Article 250, Part III, for a local grounding electrode system
requires.permitted_electrodes: any electrode or combination of electrodes described in 250.52

evidence_required: Grounding electrode system plan and details for the cell line area
Electrode type(s) identified per 250.52
Grounding and bonding one-line or riser diagram for equipment required to be grounded by Article 668

rules.title: Wire and bond fixed and portable equipment in the cell line working zone
rules.intent: Prevent hazardous potential differences when auxiliary electrical equipment is mounted on energized cell line surfaces.

connection_to_premises_wiring_by_one_of: wire or cable in suitable raceways or metal or nonmetallic cable trays; metallic systems installed with insulating breaks so they do not cause a potentially hazardous electrical condition

grounding_relaxations: ac systems supplying fixed and portable equipment within the working zone not required to be grounded
exposed conductive surfaces within the working zone not required to be grounded
circuit protection not required for control and instrumentation totally within the working zone

Bonding details for fixed equipment mounted on energized conductive surfaces

rules.title: Use compliant wiring methods between electrolyte tank equipment and conversion equipment
rules.intent: Ensure electroplating process conductors are protected from damage and accidental contact, with stricter guarding above 60 volts dc.

requires.systems_dc_voltage_>_60v: insulated conductors permitted on insulated supports provided they are protected from physical damage; bare copper or aluminum conductors permitted where supported on insulators and guarded against accidental contact up to the point of termination in accordance with 110.27

Support and insulator details for bare or insulated conductors

Warning sign locations for bare conductors (per 669.7)

rules.title: Apply Article 670 to industrial machinery supply conductors, nameplate data, and overcurrent protection
rules.intent: Establish the scope of industrial machinery requirements, whose supply-terminal equipment workspace is governed by 110.26.

covered_topics: size and overcurrent protection of supply conductors to industrial machinery

Equipment layout showing workspace at supply conductor terminal equipment per 110.26

rules.title: Ground and bond feeder-supplied buildings or structures per 250.32

Grounding/bonding detail at the mobile home service disconnect or site-isolating device
Site plan identifying distribution point and buildings served

rules.title: Apply 404.14 rating rules to snap switches controlling lighting and motor loads

Connected load per switched circuit (lighting or motor nameplate)
Manufacturer cut sheets showing switch type (ac general-use, ac-dc, etc.)

rules.title: Install metal faceplates in mobile homes per 404.9(B)

Wiring detail showing equipment grounding conductor termination at switch/receptacle yokes
Listing information for grounding-type devices used with metal faceplates

rules.title: Provide outdoor receptacles at mobile homes complying with 406.9

Cut sheets for weather-resistant receptacles and in-use (extra-duty) covers
Elevation/plan showing receptacle mounting height and exposure

Manufacturer listing data for switches

rules.intent: Ensure each mobile home has enough dedicated branch circuits for lighting, small-appliance, laundry, general appliance, and bathroom loads so circuits are not overloaded.

Appliance schedule with nameplate ratings vs circuit ratings

rules.title: Secure appliances for transit, keep appliances accessible, and use wet-location luminaires over tubs/showers
rules.intent: Prevent transit damage and shock hazards from appliances and luminaires in mobile homes, including moisture exposure at bathtubs and showers.

rules.title: Use Code wiring methods in mobile homes with cable protection and wet-location under-chassis wiring
rules.intent: Ensure mobile home wiring uses recognized methods and is protected against physical damage, stowage damage, stud penetration damage, and weather exposure under the chassis.

rules.title: Calculate mobile home supply-cord and panelboard load by the 550.18 method
rules.intent: Standardize sizing of each mobile home feeder assembly using the Article 550 calculation in lieu of Article 220 so the power supply matches the connected load.
evidence_required: Load calculation worksheet per 550.18 (or 220.82 optional method)
Floor dimensions used for lighting VA
Appliance and HVAC nameplate data
Selected feeder assembly / power-supply cord rating vs calculated amperes per leg

rules.title: Join circuits between multi-section home units with listed fixed wiring, accessible for disassembly
rules.intent: Ensure circuits spanning sections of multi-section mobile or manufactured homes are joined with approved fixed wiring methods that can be safely disassembled for relocation.
evidence_required: Crossover connection details/listing for inter-section wiring
Plan showing junction locations and access provisions
For movable expandable/multiunit homes without permanent feeders: disconnecting means and branch-circuit protection in each unit satisfying 550.10 after assembly

rules.title: List outdoor luminaires/equipment for wet locations and label outside HVAC branch-circuit connections
rules.intent: Protect outdoor electrical equipment at mobile homes from moisture and ensure field-connected outside heating/air-conditioning circuits are terminated and identified for safe connection.
evidence_required: Outdoor equipment schedule with wet/damp location listings
Detail of outside HVAC connection outlet box and permanently affixed label text
Branch-circuit rating and conductor ampacity for outside HVAC circuit

rules.title: Calculate mobile home park wiring on at least 16,000 VA per lot or the 550.18 load
rules.intent: Ensure mobile home park services and feeders are sized for the largest typical home each lot will accept, with demand factors applied only as permitted by Table 550.31.
evidence_required: Park service/feeder load calculation showing per-lot VA basis (>= 16,000 VA or 550.18 result)
Table 550.31 demand factor application by number of mobile homes
One-line diagram of park distribution with feeder and service sizes

rules.title: Locate mobile home service equipment adjacent to (not on) the home, within sight and 30 ft, rated 100 A minimum
rules.intent: Ensure a readily accessible, adequately rated service disconnect exists near each mobile home so power can be removed quickly and the feeder assembly connected by a permanent wiring method.

exceptions.note: GFCI protection is not required for the receptacle supplying the home feeder assembly.

evidence_required: Site plan showing service equipment location, sight line, and distance to home exterior wall
Service equipment rating (amperes, volts) and receptacle configuration
Grounding detail at disconnecting means per 250.32
GFCI protection specification for additional outside receptacles

rules.title: Permit service equipment in or on a manufactured home only under the seven 550.32(B) conditions
rules.intent: Allow on-unit service equipment for manufactured homes only when anchoring, service installation, grounding electrode provisions, and warning labeling ensure a safe permanent installation.
evidence_required: Manufacturer written installation instructions (anchoring/foundation, grounding method, GEC size)
Warning label text and location on or adjacent to service equipment
Service installation details showing Article 230 compliance
Grounding electrode conductor routing detail to outside the structure
